_meta.description: Safety thresholds for SafeShift sensor monitoring, based on international occupational health standards.
_meta.notes: All values represent 8-hour TWA limits unless otherwise noted. Thresholds are starting points for anomaly detection — not legal compliance tools.

sources.name: OSHA Technical Manual — Indoor Air Quality
sources.detail: OSHA recommends 68–76°F and 20–60% relative humidity for acceptable indoor air quality.

sources.name: ASHRAE Standard 55 (referenced by OSHA)
sources.detail: Thermal comfort standard for human occupancy, basis for OSHA's recommendation.

sources.name: OSHA Technical Manual — Indoor Air Quality
OSHA PEL Table Z-1 — Carbon Dioxide
sources.detail: PEL is 5,000 ppm (8-hr TWA). NIOSH REL is also 5,000 ppm with a 30,000 ppm STEL.

sources.name: OSHA CO2 Monitoring Guidelines
sources.detail: Levels above 1,000 ppm indicate inadequate ventilation in occupied spaces.

pm2_5.notes: OSHA has no PM2.5-specific PEL. The respirable fraction PEL (5 mg/m³) covers particles ≤10μm (PM10). PM2.5 falls within this but is not separately regulated.

sources.name: OSHA — Particulates Not Otherwise Regulated (PNOR)
sources.detail: Total dust PEL: 15 mg/m³. Respirable fraction PEL: 5 mg/m³.

voc.notes: No single VOC limit exists. OSHA sets PELs per compound in Table Z-1 (e.g., benzene: 1 ppm, toluene: 200 ppm). For general indoor air quality, total VOC (TVOC) below 0.5 mg/m³ is considered good.

sources.name: OSHA PEL Table Z-1 — Air Contaminants
sources.detail: Individual PELs for each VOC compound.

sources.name: OSHA — Indoor Air Quality in Commercial Buildings (OSHA 3430)
OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95 — Occupational Noise Exposure
sources.detail: PEL: 90 dBA (8-hr TWA), 5 dB exchange rate. Action level: 85 dBA triggers hearing conservation program.

sources.name: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.56 — Illumination (Construction)
sources.detail: General construction: 3 fc (~32 lux). Plants/shops: 10 fc (~110 lux). Offices: 30 fc (~320 lux).

sources.name: EU Directive 2002/44/EC — Physical Agents (Vibration)
sources.detail: HAV action: 2.5 m/s², limit: 5.0 m/s². WBV action: 0.5 m/s², limit: 1.15 m/s². All 8-hr TWA.

sources.name: ILO Convention No. 1 — Hours of Work (Industry), 1919
sources.detail: 8 hours/day, 48 hours/week. Shift work may average over 3 weeks with 56-hr weekly max.

sources.name: ILO Q&As on Business and Working Time
sources.detail: Convention No. 30 allows up to 10 hours/day if weekly total ≤48 hours.

sources.name: ETI Base Code Clause 6 — Working Hours
